title: 2017 Year in Review
summary: A year of setbacks — learning to treat friction as a habit, and fighting myself every step of the way
markdown:
2017 was a year full of setbacks. Faced with hit after hit, I went from feeling crushed to slowly treating frustration as something normal. I still haven't fully left that shadow behind — but I believe the light comes back eventually. Spring always does.

Looking back, here's what I did for myself in 2017:

1. Started this blog. Writing forces me to turn what I've learned into something I can share — and it locks the theory in my own head at the same time.
1. Went deep on core JavaScript. In this field, the fundamentals matter more than the flavor of the week. I spent a lot of time on core concepts so I could actually write better code.
1. Explored IoT. It felt like the future, so I put time into the related stack. I understand the space better now, and I'm better prepared for what comes next.
1. Stuck with the Dedao app ("Got It" / 得到). It's a steady stream of material adjacent to what I do, and it raised both how much I notice and how efficiently I learn.

Looking ahead to 2018, a few small targets:

1. Keep going deeper on JavaScript fundamentals. Language core knowledge isn't optional for where I want my career to go.
1. Consolidate theory by sharing. Blog posts, forums — teach what I learn. It helps me, and it might help someone else.
1. Face the English problem. It's been a wall for a long time. My plan: translate something every day, even if it's only one sentence. Consistency beats intensity.
1. Contribute to open source. Good practice for coding and for collaboration. I want to work with better developers and level up by proximity.

2018 will be full of opportunity and friction in equal measure. I believe steady learning is still the path. Here's to whatever comes next.
